name: Fields with .name
key_idea: `.` is the whole input. `.name` reads one field of an object, and `.a.b` goes one level deeper. A field that is missing gives `null`.

name: Array Items by Index
key_idea: `.[0]` is the first item of an array and `.[-1]` is the last. `.[1:3]` is a slice: a shorter array.

name: Chain Filters with |
key_idea: `a | b` runs `a`, then runs `b` on what `a` gave. Build a long filter from small steps.

name: Every Item with .[]
key_idea: `.[]` gives every item of an array as its own output. What follows the pipe then runs once for each item.

name: Missing Data with ?
key_idea: `?` after a step hides its error: `.a?` gives nothing when the input is not an object. Without `?`, jq stops with an error.

name: Collect into an Array with [ ]
key_idea: `[ ... ]` collects every output of the filter inside it into one array. `[.[] | .name]` turns many outputs back into one value.

name: Build Objects with { }
key_idea: `{name: .user, id: .id}` builds a new object. `{id}` is short for `{id: .id}`.

name: Several Outputs with ,
key_idea: `a, b` gives the outputs of `a`, then the outputs of `b`. Use it to read several things from one input.

name: Text with \( )
key_idea: Inside a string, `\(filter)` is replaced by the filter's output. `"\(.name) is \(.age)"` builds text from fields.

name: Change Every Item with map
key_idea: `map(f)` runs `f` on every item of an array and gives a new array. It is short for `[.[] | f]`.

name: Keep Items with select
key_idea: `select(test)` passes a value on when the test is true and drops it when the test is false. Use it on a stream of items, after `.[]` or inside `map`.

name: Count with length
key_idea: `length` is the number of items in an array, of keys in an object, or of characters in a string. To count matches, keep them first, then take the length.

name: Plain Text with -r
key_idea: jq prints strings as JSON, with quotes. The `-r` flag prints them as plain text, ready for the shell.

name: One Line per Value with -c
key_idea: jq pretty-prints by default. The `-c` flag prints each output value on one line, which is what line-based tools need.

name: Pass Values with --arg
key_idea: `--arg name value` gives the filter a string variable `$name`. `--argjson` passes a JSON value. With `-n`, jq runs with no input.

name: Many Inputs with -s
key_idea: A file may hold many JSON values, one per line. jq runs the filter once per value. The `-s` flag reads them all into one array first.

name: Defaults with //
key_idea: `a // b` gives `a`, unless `a` is `null` or `false`; then it gives `b`. Use it for a default value.

name: Maths and + on Each Type
key_idea: `+` adds numbers, joins strings, joins arrays and merges objects. `-`, `*`, `/` and `%` work on numbers.

name: Tests with ==, < and and
key_idea: `==`, `!=`, `<`, `>=` compare two values and give `true` or `false`. `and`, `or` and `not` combine tests.

name: Choose with if
key_idea: `if test then a else b end` gives `a` when the test is true and `b` otherwise. `elif` adds more cases.

name: Object Keys with keys and has
key_idea: `keys` gives the keys of an object as a sorted array. `has("k")` tests whether a key exists, even when its value is `null`.

name: Check Types with type
key_idea: `type` gives the kind of a value as a string: `"number"`, `"string"`, `"array"`, `"object"`, `"boolean"` or `"null"`.

name: Split and Join Strings
key_idea: `split(",")` cuts a string into an array of parts. `join(",")` glues an array of strings into one string.

name: Match Text with test
key_idea: `test("regex")` is true when the string matches. `startswith`, `endswith` and `contains` cover the simple cases.

name: Replace Text with sub and gsub
key_idea: `sub("a"; "b")` replaces the first match and `gsub` replaces every match. `ascii_downcase` and `ascii_upcase` change the case.

name: Convert with tostring and tonumber
key_idea: `tostring` turns any value into a string and `tonumber` turns a numeric string into a number. jq never converts by itself.

name: Rows with @csv and @tsv
key_idea: `@csv` and `@tsv` turn an array into one line of a table. Use them with `-r`, so the line is printed as plain text.

name: Sort with sort and sort_by
key_idea: `sort` orders an array. `sort_by(.field)` orders objects by a field. `reverse` turns the order around.

name: Totals with add, min and max
key_idea: `add` adds up every item of an array. `min` and `max` give the smallest and largest; `min_by(.f)` and `max_by(.f)` compare by a field.

name: Unique Values with unique
key_idea: `unique` sorts an array and removes repeats. `unique_by(.field)` keeps one object for each value of the field.

name: Group with group_by
key_idea: `group_by(.field)` splits an array into an array of groups: one array for each value of the field. Then `map` each group to a summary.

name: Objects as Lists with to_entries
key_idea: `to_entries` turns an object into an array of `{key, value}` pairs, and `from_entries` turns it back. `with_entries(f)` does both around `f`.

name: Change in Place with |=
key_idea: `path |= f` replaces the value at the path with `f` of the old value and keeps everything else. `=` sets a fixed value and `+=` adds to it.

name: Remove with del
key_idea: `del(path)` gives the input without the value at that path. It removes keys from objects and items from arrays.

name: Find Anything with ..
key_idea: `..` gives the input and every value inside it, at any depth. Follow it with `select` or `.key?` to find values wherever they are.

name: Name a Value with as $x
key_idea: `value as $x | ...` gives a value a name. Use it to keep something from the outer input while you work on an inner part.

name: Fold with reduce
key_idea: `reduce .[] as $x (start; update)` walks the items and carries one result along. Each step sets the result to `update`, where `.` is the result so far.

name: Your Own Filters with def
key_idea: `def name: body;` gives a filter a name, so a long program reads in small steps. `def name(f): ...;` takes a filter as an argument.
